steps: For sticking total mass is 4 kg, so common final V=+4/4=+1 m/s.
K_after=½×4×1²=2 J, so 6 J was converted during contact.
P_after=4×1=+4 kg·m/s; 6 J is not a momentum loss.
hints: Clarify: STICK imposes one common final speed; it does not imply kinetic-energy conservation.
Correlate: solve signed momentum first, then compute two kinetic energies separately.
Open the way: the 4 kg joined object moves at +1 m/s, so compare initial 8 J with final 2 J.

diagnostics.joinedV: The contact law is sticking, not elastic scattering; use common final velocity.
diagnostics.totalP: Check signed total momentum: no external impulse acts in the short contact.
diagnostics.loss: Recompute K_after for the full 4 kg joined mass; don't equate momentum and energy.

boundarySteps: Ideal elasticity adds conservation of total kinetic energy to P=+4 kg·m/s.
The unequal-mass 1D elastic solution is v_A=−2 m/s, v_B=+2 m/s.
